chunks: And by his chain, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a mother of a child (Umm al-Walad) of a Christian man who became a Muslim, can the Muslim man marry her? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, and her waiting period (Iddah) from the Christian man, when she becomes a Muslim, is the waiting period of a free divorced woman, being three months or three pure periods (Quroo'). So when her waiting period is completed, let him marry her if she desires.

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a female slave who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a Christian slave woman who converts to Islam and wishes to marry a Muslim?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a Christian concubine (Umm Walad) who converts to Islam is entitled to marry her Muslim master, with her waiting period (Iddah) calculated from the time of her conversion rather than her divorce. This ruling aligns her status with that of a free divorced woman, requiring either three menstrual cycles or three lunar months, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that conversion severs the previous non-Muslim marital bond. The narration underscores the legal transition from slavery to freedom and the subsequent eligibility for permanent marriage within the Islamic framework.
